claim: A 2025 study reported an eight-week human iPSC-derived glia-enriched organoid containing neurons, astrocytes, oligodendrocyte-lineage cells, myelinating oligodendrocytes, and microglia, and used inflammatory stimuli plus orthogonal imaging and single-cell readouts as a technical model of progression-relevant glial responses.
future_grounding_route: Use only as platform context. A project experiment would require independent donors, crossed microglial and neural backgrounds, randomized blinded perturbation, donor-level inference, a frozen functional-rescue gate, and independent replication.

project_finding_reference.finding_id: no portable progression state or intervention route in held data

project_use: External technical precedent for a human multicellular progression assay; not evidence that senescence, any named drug, or any target is a project finding.
relationship_note: The platform can measure microglial state and oligodendrocyte/myelin consequences in one human model, but the source's three iPSC lines, incomplete myelin compaction, and short microglial persistence limit transfer.

source.citation: Fagiani et al. Spatially-restricted inflammation-induced senescent-like glia in multiple sclerosis and patient-derived organoids. Nature Communications. 2025.
source.label: MS glia-enriched organoid model

source_terms.license_or_terms_label: Publisher page metadata and short paraphrase only
source_terms.reuse_notes: Store bibliographic metadata and a short paraphrase; do not redistribute article text or figures.

why_unverifiable: The project has not reproduced the organoid platform or independently rerun its source data and pharmacological experiments.
